# iliad-089 (14.329–432) — new renderings chosen

No departure from the Odyssey table or the Iliad table. Every repeated whole unit (14.329, 330, 341, 356, 370, 378) takes the published English exactly; lines repeated inside longer units (14.380, 408, 430–431, 432) reuse the published wording; νεμεσσητὸν δέ κεν εἴη keeps the published "it would be a thing to resent" / "that would be a thing to resent" (iliad-020, odyssey-110).

Choices below are new to the table. "Stock" marks those likely to recur.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided, and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| μενέχαρμος (376, ἀνὴρ μενέχαρμος) — stock | "steadfast in the fight" | "steadfast in battle" | "bold", "stout-hearted" (lose μένω "stand fast"); μένω + χάρμη "battle" |
| παναίθῃσιν κορύθεσσι (372) | "all-blazing helmets" | "blazing helmets" | "gleaming" (reserved for γλαυκῶπις), "shining" (φαεινός), "flashing" (νώροπα, ἀστεροπητής); πᾶν + αἴθω "burn" |
| νεοθηλέα ποίην (347) | "new-sprouting grass" | "newly sprouting grass" | "fresh", "tender" (τέρην is "tender"); νέος + θάλλω |
| χθὼν δῖα (347) | "the heavenly earth" | "the heavenly earth" | "divine earth"; follows δῖος "heavenly" (even of the sea, ἅλα δῖαν) |
| ὑάκινθος, κρόκος (348) | "hyacinth", "crocus" | same | the note says what the first plant was is not certain |
| ὃς ἀπὸ χθονὸς ὑψόσ’ ἔεργε (349) | "which up from the ground kept them aloft" | "which kept them high above the ground" | "held them apart", "shut them off"; ἔργω "keep (away)" with ὑψόσε "on high"; the Greek gives no object, "them" is the pair |
| ἐπὶ δὲ νεφέλην ἕσσαντο (350) | "over themselves put on a cloud" | "put a beautiful golden cloud on over themselves" | "wrapped themselves in"; ἕννυμι "put on, clothe" |
| στιλπναὶ … ἔερσαι (351) | "glistening dews" | "glistening drops of dew" | "bright", "shining" (reserved for φαεινός) |
| ἀτρέμας εὗδε πατήρ (352; Zeus unnamed) | "motionless slept, the father" | "slept motionless … the father" | "Father Zeus" (the Greek withholds the name until 359); ἀτρέμας keeps the table's "motionless" |
| Γαργάρῳ ἄκρῳ (352) | "topmost Gargarus" | "the peak of Gargarus" | "the summit"; ἄκρος "topmost" |
| ὕπνῳ καὶ φιλότητι δαμείς (353) | "overcome by sleep and love" | same | "tamed", "subdued", "conquered" |
| ἀγγελίην ἐρέων (355) | "news to tell" | "to tell the news" | "bearing a message"; ἐρέω "say, tell"; ἀγγελίη "news" (table) |
| κῦδος ὄπαζε (358) | "grant … glory" | "grant them glory" | "bestow", "make follow"; follows the table's ὤπασαν "granted" |
| μίνυνθά περ (358) | "for a little while at least" | "if only for a little while" | "briefly" (the table's μίνυνθα); περ "at least" |
| μαλακὸν … κῶμα (359) | "soft slumber" | "soft slumber" | "coma" (a loan), "deep sleep"; κῶμα "slumber" kept apart from ὕπνος "sleep" |
| Ἥρη … παρήπαφεν εὐνηθῆναι (360) | "Hera in love has beguiled him to lie down" | "Hera, in love, has beguiled him into lying down" | Hera is the subject; εὐνηθῆναι "to lie down" is the same word as at 331 |
| ὣς εἰπὼν ὃ μὲν ᾤχετ’ ἐπὶ κλυτὰ φῦλ’ ἀνθρώπων (361) | "So having spoken, he went off to the famous tribes of men" | "So he spoke, and went off to the famous tribes of men" | "peoples", "nations" (ἔθνος); φῦλον "tribe"; ὣς εἰπών "so having spoken" as in the table |
| τὸν δ’ ἔτι μᾶλλον ἀνῆκεν (362) | "and him still more he urged on" | "and urged him on still more" | "set on", "stirred up"; follows the Odyssey's 6.256 "urged" |
| αὐτίκα δ’ ἐν πρώτοισι μέγα προθορὼν ἐκέλευσεν (363, whole line) | "At once among the first, greatly leaping forward, he bade:" | "At once he leapt far forward among the foremost and bade them:" | "urged", "cried"; ἐκέλευσεν "bade" (κελεύω keeps "bid"); ἐν πρώτοισι follows προμάχοισι "foremost" |
| μεθίεμεν … νίκην Ἕκτορι (364) | "let go the victory to Hector" | "hand the victory over to Hector" | "give up", "slacken from" (the table's μεθίημι with the genitive); here accusative and dative |
| καὶ δ’ αὖτε (364) | "and further, again" | "once again" | "and also"; read as a reproach |
| εὔχεται (366) | "vaunts" | "boasts" | "prays" (the table's εὔχομαι of prayer, 1.43); here the sense is plainly boasting |
| κεχολωμένος ἦτορ (367) | "angered in heart" | "angered at heart" | "incensed" (kept for χωόμενος κῆρ / χώσατο); χολόω "anger" |
| κείνου … ποθή (368) | "no very great lack" | "no great lack of him" | table's ποθή "lack" |
| ὀτρυνώμεθ’ … ἀλλήλοισιν (369) | "urge ourselves on … for one another" | "urge one another on … each other" | "rouse"; table's ὀτρύνω "urge" |
| ἀσπίδες ὅσσαι ἄρισται … ἠδὲ μέγισται (371) | "the shields that are best … and greatest" | "the best and biggest shields" | "finest", "largest" |
| κεφαλὰς κρύψαντες (372) | "our heads … having hidden" | "cover our heads" | "protected", "shielded" |
| ἔγχε’ ἑλόντες (373) | "spears having taken" | "take … spears in our hands" | "grasp", "seize" |
| χείρονι φωτί (377) | "to a worse man" | "to a worse man" | "weaker", "lesser" (each decides in which respect); χείρων "worse" |
| ἐν ἀσπίδι μείζονι δύτω (377) | "let him get inside the bigger shield" | "get into a bigger shield" | "hide behind", "take cover in" |
| ἀρήϊα τεύχεα ἄμειβον (381) | "warlike armour they exchanged" | "exchanged the warlike armour" | "swapped", "traded"; ἀρήϊος "warlike", τεύχεα "armour" (table) |
| ἐσθλὰ μὲν ἐσθλὸς ἔδυνε, χέρεια δὲ χείρονι δόσκεν (382, whole line) | "good things the good man put on, and worse things to the worse man he gave" | "The good man put on the good armour, and gave the worse armour to the worse man" | "the brave", "the noble"; the iterative δόσκεν is not marked in English, the note says it |
| βάν ῥ’ ἴμεν (384) | "they set off to go" | "they set out" | "went forth"; βάν "they went" + ἴμεν "to go" |
| δεινὸν ἄορ τανύηκες (385) | "a dread sword, long-pointed" | "a dread, long-pointed sword" | table's τανύηκες "long-pointed" |
| εἴκελον ἀστεροπῇ (386) | "like lightning" | "like lightning" | "like a flash of lightning"; ἀστεροπή "lightning" (table's ἀστεροπητής) |
| τῷ δ’ οὐ θέμις ἐστὶ μιγῆναι ἐν δαῒ λευγαλέῃ (386–387) | "with which it is not right to be mingled in pitiful battle" | "It is not right to meet it in pitiful battle" | "grievous" (reserved for ἀλεγεινός), "wretched"; λευγαλέος "pitiful" (table); δαΐς "battle"; the note says τῷ may be "him" |
| δέος ἰσχάνει ἄνδρας (387) | "fear holds men back" | "fear holds men back" | "restrains", "checks" |
| κυανοχαῖτα Ποσειδάων (390; nominative) — stock | "dark-haired Poseidon" | "dark-haired Poseidon" | "blue-maned", "dark-maned"; the table's κυανοχαῖτα "dark-haired one" (9.528, vocative) |
| αἰνοτάτην ἔριδα πτολέμοιο τάνυσσαν (389) | "the most dread strife of war they stretched" | "stretched out the most dreadful strife of war" | "drew tight", "pulled"; τανύω "stretch"; ἔρις "strife", αἰνός "dread" |
| ξύνισαν μεγάλῳ ἀλαλητῷ (393) | "brought themselves together with a great outcry" | "met with a great outcry" | "clashed"; table's ἀλαλητός "outcry"; ξυνίημι "bring together" (1.8) |
| πνοιῇ Βορέω ἀλεγεινῇ (395) | "the grievous breath of the North Wind" | "the grievous breath of the North Wind" | "blast" (reserved for ἄελλα); table's πνοιή "breath", Βορέης "North Wind", ἀλεγεινός "grievous" |
| βρόμος (396) | "roar" | "roar" | "crackling", "din" |
| ἠπύει (399) | "cry aloud" | "cry aloud" | "howl", "whistle"; ἠπύω "call aloud" (table's ἠπύτα) |
| χαλεπαίνων (399) | "growing harsh" | "in its fury" | table's χαλεπαίνων "growing harsh" / "in my anger" |
| δεινὸν ἀϋσάντων (401) | "shouting fearsomely" | "shouting fearsomely" | "dreadfully", "terribly" (turned down for δεινόν as adverb in the table, 4.420) |
| ἀργυροήλου (405) | "silver-studded" | "silver-studded" | "silver-nailed", "silver-hilted"; ἦλος "stud, nail" |
| τελαμῶνε (404) | "the two straps" | "the two straps" | "baldrics"; follows iliad-034's "strap" |
| ῥυσάσθην τέρενα χρόα (406) | "protected … the tender skin" | "protected his tender skin" | "saved"; table's ῥύομαι "protect", τέρενα χρόα "tender skin" |
| ὅττί ῥά οἱ βέλος ὠκὺ ἐτώσιον ἔκφυγε χειρός (407) | "the swift shaft in vain had flown from his hand" | "his swift shaft had flown from his hand in vain" | "missile", "dart"; table's βέλος "shaft", ἐτώσιον "in vain" |
| στρόμβον δ’ ὣς ἔσσευε βαλών (413) | "like a top he set him whirling" | "set him spinning like a top" | "whirlwind", "pine cone"; στρόμβος "top" |
| ὑπὲρ ἄντυγος (412) | "above the rim" | "above the rim of his shield" | "above the edge", "over the rail"; ἄντυξ "rim" |
| θεείου … ὀδμή (415) | "smell of sulphur" | "smell of sulphur" | "brimstone", "stench"; table's θέειον "sulphur" |
| χαλεπὸς … κεραυνός (417) | "harsh is the thunderbolt" | "harsh is the thunderbolt" | "dreadful", "cruel"; χαλεπός "harsh" |
| ὣς ἔπεσ’ Ἕκτορος ὦκα χαμαὶ μένος (418, whole line) | "so fell of Hector swiftly to the ground the might in the dust" | "so the might of Hector fell quickly to the ground in the dust" | "strength", "spirit" (μένος is "might", table) |
| ἰάχοντες … ἐρύεσθαι (421) | "shouting loudly … to drag him away" | "shouting loudly … to drag him away" | "to rescue"; ἐρύω "drag" |
| θαμειὰς αἰχμάς (422–423) | "thick spear-points" | "spears thick and fast" | "dense", "close-packed"; αἰχμή "spear-point" |
| Πουλυδάμας (425) | "Polydamas" | "Polydamas" | "Poulydamas" (the edition's spelling); familiar English form |
| Σαρπηδών τ’ ἀρχὸς Λυκίων (426) | "Sarpedon, commander of the Lycians" | same | "leader" (ἡγήτωρ); table's ἀρχός "commander" |
| Γλαῦκος ἀμύμων (426) | "Glaucus, blameless" | "blameless Glaucus" | "peerless", "noble"; table's ἀμύμων "blameless" |
| οὔ τίς εὑ ἀκήδεσεν (427) | "none neglected him" | "none neglected him" | "cared for him not at all"; table's ἀκηδής "uncared for" |
| ἀσπίδας εὐκύκλους σχέθον αὐτοῦ (428) | "held their well-rounded shields right there" | "held their well-rounded shields in front of him, right there" | "shielded him"; table's σχέθον "held", εὔκυκλος "well-rounded" |
| χερσὶν ἀείραντες φέρον ἐκ πόνου (429) | "with their hands lifting bore out of the toil" | "lifted him in their hands and carried him out of the toil" | "from the fight" (πόνος is "toil", table) |
